engines.name: Kernighan/Pike TPOP matcher (Beautiful Code ch.1)
engines.algorithm: recursive backtracking directly over the pattern string (match/matchhere/matchstar)
engines.features: literal, ., ^, $, c* only; no classes, no |, no groups, no {n,m}, no lazy, no UTF-8, no icase
engines.notes: Root of the whole 'tiny regex' lineage (kokke, cregex, torstenvl, Espruino). Pedagogical baseline, not a usable engine.

engines.name: kokke/tiny-regex-c
engines.algorithm: compile pattern into fixed array of 30 tokens (no malloc), then Pike-style backtracking matchpattern/matchstar/matchplus over tokens (iterative search loop by default)
engines.features: ., ^, $, *, +, ? (greedy quantifiers; no lazy), [abc] [^abc] [a-z], \d\w\s+negations; NO |, NO groups/captures, NO {n,m}, NO UTF-8 (bytes), NO icase. README: inverted classes buggy, BRANCH commented out in re.c
engines.maintained: last commit 2024-10-25; author 'will accept patches'; HN thread 2020
engines.claimed_size: README: '500 SLOC, ~3kb binary for x86'; 'gcc -Os -c re.c: text 2404 bss 304' (x86 gcc 7.2)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1532 B incl. re_print 162 B -> ~1.37 KB. Smallest widely used engine; ASCII-only, no |, groups, {n,m}. Forks catalogued separately: rurban, ximtech, zeta-zero, tiny-regex-mod, gyrovorbis (platformio_tiny-regex, CrackerCat, liukangcc are plain mirrors).

engines.name: rurban/tiny-regex-c (extended fork)
engines.algorithm: same as kokke (token array + backtracking), extended
engines.features: kokke set + {n} {n,} {,m} {n,m}, \xXX, | branch, (...) group (no capture API), optional _UNICODE wchar build; no lazy, no icase
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2927 B incl. re_print 347 B -> ~2.58 KB. cbmc/KLEE harness included.

engines.name: zeta-zero/tiny-regex-c
engines.algorithm: tokenised pattern + backtracking matcher, kokke-inspired rewrite; configurable via TINY_REGEX_CONFIG_* macros
engines.features: ., ^, $, |, *, +, ?, {n,m}, [] [^], \d\w\s+neg, () limited ('no support (..|..) and ((...)?(...)*)+'); returns match span only (no per-group captures); no lazy, no UTF-8, no icase; nesting depth 8, max 9 alternatives
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1865 B (all features). Claims 'most rules supported' but groups+alternation combination unsupported.

engines.name: ximtech/Regex (tiny-regex-c refactor)
engines.algorithm: kokke design refactored: compiled token array + backtracking; static allocation removed (caller-provided Regex struct)
engines.features: ., ^, $, * + ? with lazy *? +? (? documented lazy), {m,n} {m} {m,}, [] [^] ranges, \d\w\s+neg; NO |, NO groups/captures, NO UTF-8, NO icase
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2355 B. Perl-test-based coverage. Used from STM32/CLion CPM examples.

engines.name: mattbucknall/subreg
engines.algorithm: recursive-descent matcher directly over the pattern string, NON-backtracking (greedy/possessive only), anchored-only (^ $ implied); no compile step
engines.features: ., \n\t etc, \d\w\s\h + negations, [] [^] ranges, ? * + (greedy/possessive), |, () (?:...) captures, (?= (?! lookahead, \i/\I in-pattern nocase toggles; NO {n,m}, NO lazy, NO search (anchored), ASCII only
engines.maintained: last commit 2025-10-18; author calls it feature-complete
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1704 B. Non-backtracking means 'a*a' style patterns fail (possessive semantics) - will diverge from Python/JS corpus a lot.

engines.name: cesanta/slre
engines.algorithm: recursive matcher directly over the pattern string (bar/doh/baz functions) with a pre-pass that indexes brackets and | branches; no bytecode
engines.features: ^ $ . () captures, |, [] [^] ranges, \s\S\d, \xHH, \n\r\t.., + +? * *? ? (lazy variants), SLRE_IGNORE_CASE flag (ASCII); NO {n,m}, NO \w, NO (?:), NO UTF-8 ('under development' since 2013)
engines.maintained: core unchanged since ~2013; last commit 2026-08-26 (typo); 16 open issues
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1946 B. Used in Mongoose/V7. GPL blocks closed firmware. Pre-2013 SLRE 1.0 was a different bytecode design.

engines.name: T-Rex (Alberto Demichelis)
engines.url: https://tiny-rex.sourceforge.net/ (source mirror: https://github.com/kimperator/T-Rex; identical copy in Squirrel sqstdlib/sqstdrex.cpp)
engines.algorithm: parse to node array (malloc'd), recursive backtracking matcher over nodes (trex_matchnode); setjmp error handling
engines.features: ., ^, $, |, () captures, (?:), [] ranges/negation, \w\d\s\a\x\c\p\l\u + uppercase negations, \b, * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} (greedy only); NO lazy, NO icase, 8-bit or UTF-16 (_UNICODE) chars, NO UTF-8
engines.maintained: 2003-2006 (v1.3); unmaintained standalone but alive inside Squirrel (commit 2026-02)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2925 B (5 malloc calls). diff vs Squirrel's sqstdrex.cpp is whitespace-only. Also wrapped by CZMQ zrex.

engines.name: omtinez/tiny-rex (T-Rex for AVR)
engines.algorithm: T-Rex trimmed
engines.features: T-Rex feature set
engines.claimed_size: README: 'For AVR ... binary size is under 8K'
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2660 B (vs 2925 B original).

engines.name: pfalcon/re1.5 (MicroPython/Berry 're')
engines.algorithm: single-pass compile to compact bytecode (Char/Any/Class/NamedClass/Split/RSplit/Jmp/Save/Match); backends: recursive backtracking (recursiveloop.c), backtracking VM (backtrack.c), Pike VM (pike.c)
engines.features: literal, ., ^, $, [] [^] ranges, \d\s\w+neg, * + ? with lazy ??/*?/+?, |, () captures, (?:); NO {n,m} (RE1_5_UNSUPPORTED_SYNTAX), NO UTF-8 (byte-wise), NO icase, NO named groups
engines.maintained: last commit 2019-05-05; lives on as micropython/lib/re1.5 (diverged fork with EMIT_CHECKED overflow checks, 2026) and Berry/Tasmota 're' module (docs fetched)
engines.claimed_size: README: 'minimal code size and memory use', no numbers
engines.source_files: compilecode.c charclass.c + one of backtrack.c/recursiveloop.c/pike.c (+sub.c util.c); re1.5.h
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: compilecode 1102 + charclass 126 + backtrack 477 (recursiveloop 336, pike 680) + sub 126 + util 99 -> ~1.9 KB compile+backtrack. The one real-world MCU regex (MicroPython 'ure'); caller supplies the bytecode buffer.

engines.name: kyx0r/pikevm (re1.5 + UTF-8 + {n,m})
engines.algorithm: compile to int-sized code, Pike VM only (lockstep thread lists, O(n*m)), no backtracking
engines.features: re1.5 set + {n} {n,m} {n,}, UTF-8 (byte offsets out), (?:), \< \> word assertions; icase/NOTBOL/lookaround only in nextvi branch (regex.c); no malloc (caller buffers)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 (main separated via -fno-inline-functions-called-once): compilecode 1872 + re_pikevm 1668 + reg_comp 170 + isword 32 = ~3.7 KB + 256 B data (utf8 length table). Closest existing engine to the spike's list, but README describes POSIX-ish leftmost-longest submatch fix.

engines.name: rsc/re1 (Russ Cox 'Regular Expression Matching: the VM approach')
engines.algorithm: yacc parser -> AST -> Inst array; backends: recursive, backtracking VM (thread stack), Pike VM, Thompson NFA
engines.features: literal, ., |, () captures, (?:), * + ? with lazy variants; NO character classes, NO ^ $, NO \d\w\s, NO {n,m}, NO UTF-8, NO icase; malloc
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 with bison-generated parser: parse 1715 + compile 759 + sub 126 + backtrack 267 / pike 492 / recursive 316. Toy; re1.5 is the practical descendant.

engines.name: Henry Spencer regexp(3) 1986 ('book' library)
engines.algorithm: compile to linear NFA byte program (BRANCH/BACK/STAR/PLUS/EXACTLY/ANYOF nodes, 2-byte next offsets) + recursive backtracking regmatch; regstart/regmust prefilters
engines.features: egrep style: literal . ^ $ [] ranges/negation, * + ?, |, () captures (9); NO {n,m}, NO lazy, NO \d\w\s, NO icase, byte-wise; malloc for program
engines.license: custom permissive (U of Toronto; may redistribute, no misrepresentation)
engines.maintained: historical 1986/1995 (ancestors of Tcl7, Apache 1.x, early vim, Perl 1)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2751 B. Design blueprint for most backtracking engines.

engines.name: Henry Spencer 1994 BSD regex (POSIX)
engines.algorithm: POSIX ERE/BRE; NFA program + engine.c matcher (backtracking with 'slow'/'fast' DFA-ish stepping)
engines.features: POSIX BRE/ERE incl. {n,m}, [[:class:]], backrefs, REG_ICASE; leftmost-longest; no lazy, byte-wise
engines.notes: Scale reference for 'libc regex'. Not measured (POSIX semantics, >5 KB expected).

engines.name: Plan 9 libregexp (Rob Pike) / plan9port / 0intro Unix port
engines.algorithm: operator-precedence parser -> NFA instruction array; regexec runs Pike-VM style lockstep thread lists (leftmost-longest), UTF-8 Runes
engines.features: literal . ^ $ [] ranges/negation, * + ?, |, () captures (32); NO {n,m}, NO lazy, NO \d\w\s, NO icase; malloc for program; file-scope statics in regcomp (not reentrant)
engines.license: MIT (Plan 9 Foundation 2021) / Lucent Public License historically
engines.source_files: regcomp.c regexec.c regaux.c regcomp.h regexp9.h (+rregexec.c for Rune input, regsub.c)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: regcomp 2159 + regexec 736 + regaux 340 = ~3.2 KB. Leftmost-longest semantics differ from Perl/JS; UTF-8 handled natively. mujs regexp.c is a descendant.

engines.name: 9front libregexp (rewrite)
engines.algorithm: recursive-descent parser (e0..e3) -> Renode tree -> Reinst array; thread-list executor (Rethread, NSUBEXPM=32)
engines.features: same Plan 9 syntax (. ^ $ [] * + ? | ()), UTF-8 Runes, regcomplit literal mode; no {n,m}, no lazy, no \d\w\s, no icase; malloc
engines.maintained: active (mirror commit 2026-09-03, Ori Bernstein); original rewrite author/date unverified
engines.notes: Not measured: needs u.h/libc.h. Cleaner than the Bell Labs version but same semantics.

engines.name: mujs regexp.c (Tor Andersson, Artifex MuJS)
engines.algorithm: recursive-descent parser -> AST -> instruction array (Plan 9 lineage); recursive backtracking match() with depth limit REG_MAXREC and REG_RUNAWAY step limit; setjmp errors
engines.features: JS RegExp subset: . ^ $ [] ranges/negation, \d\w\s+neg, \b \B, backrefs, * + ? {m,n} greedy+lazy, |, () (?:) (?= (?!, captures (16), REG_ICASE (Unicode via toupperrune), REG_NEWLINE; UTF-8 (Rune-based)
engines.notes: Standalone-able (needs utf.c). Measured Cortex-M4: regexp.c text=5369 B; chartorune+runetochar ~0.3 KB; ~13 KB Unicode case/alpha tables pulled in only by icase/Unicode \w. Allocator hook (regcompx) but needs heap.

engines.name: QuickJS libregexp (Fabrice Bellard)
engines.algorithm: direct bytecode generation (no parse tree); backtracking with explicit stack (no C recursion); simple quantifiers optimised
engines.features: full ES2025 RegExp: classes, Unicode props, named groups, lookbehind, backrefs, sticky, v-flag sets, {n,m}, lazy, icase (Unicode)
engines.claimed_size: doc/quickjs.texi: 'The full regexp library weights about 15 KiB (x86 code), excluding the Unicode library'
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: libregexp.c 13.3 KB, libunicode.c 49 KB (tables), cutils.c 2.1 KB. Scale reference for 'complete JS regex'. kmarius/jsregexp wraps it for Lua; MicroQuickJS's derived engine is catalogued separately.

engines.name: musl libc regex (TRE-derived)
engines.algorithm: TRE tagged-NFA (TNFA) parallel matcher, linear-time; POSIX regcomp/regexec
engines.features: POSIX BRE/ERE + {n,m}, [[:class:]], backrefs, REG_ICASE, REG_NEWLINE; multibyte/UTF-8 via mbrtowc; leftmost-longest; no lazy; malloc
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 (musl headers): regcomp 9285 + regexec 3792 + tre-mem 232 = ~13.3 KB. Upstream TRE (laurikari/tre, 6172 sloc, BSD-2) adds approximate matching. Newlib/picolibc ship NO regex, which is why MCU projects go looking for these engines.

engines.name: Oniguruma
engines.algorithm: backtracking with optimisations; multiple syntaxes
engines.features: Perl/Ruby/Java/Python syntaxes, many encodings incl. UTF-8, Unicode props, lookaround, backrefs, named groups
engines.notes: Scale reference (Ruby's engine). Not measured.

engines.name: PCRE2
engines.algorithm: backtracking (interpretive) + optional JIT
engines.features: full Perl syntax; UTF-8/16/32; --disable-unicode shrinks
engines.notes: Scale reference; typically hundreds of KB. Not measured.

engines.name: RE2
engines.algorithm: automata: lazy DFA, NFA (Pike), onepass, bitstate; no backtracking
engines.features: RE2 syntax, Unicode, no backrefs
engines.notes: Scale reference only (C++, needs heap and abseil).

engines.name: jserv/cregex
engines.algorithm: shunting-yard parser -> AST -> Pike VM (lockstep thread list with captures, O(n*m)); malloc in parse/compile/vm
engines.features: ^ $ . [] [^] ranges, ? * + {x,y} greedy and lazy (??, *?, +?, {x,y}?), () captures, | (in parse.c); NO \d\w\s, NO (?:), NO UTF-8, NO icase; 'subset of POSIX BRE' semantics claimed but engine is leftmost-first Pike VM
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: parse 1068 + compile 994 + vm 542 = ~2.6 KB. Tested against Go's regexp test data. Good structural reference for a lockstep design with lazy quantifiers.

engines.name: wareya/Remimu (single-header)
engines.algorithm: pattern -> token array; backtracking with explicit length-checked fixed buffers (no recursion, no heap); 'O(2^x) worst case' per README
engines.features: {n,m}, * + ? greedy/lazy/possessive, atomic groups, | () (?:) captures, [] ranges, \d\s\w+neg, \b \B, \xHH, ^ $; 8-bit only (bytes; UTF-8 via external tool), NO icase, NO backrefs/lookaround, no search API (match at index)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 via wrapper TU: text=7345 B. Validated against PCRE2 in its test matrix.

engines.name: deinernstjetzt/mregexp
engines.algorithm: compiled node tree on heap, backtracking matcher; UTF-8 decoding
engines.features: . * + {m,n} | () [] [^] \d\s\w+neg \n\t\r; UTF-8 aware, byte offsets; ? not documented, no lazy, no icase, no captures API
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2550 B. Needs malloc.

engines.name: marchelzo/libre
engines.algorithm: regex AST -> Thompson NFA, NFA simulation (state sets)
engines.features: literal . [] [^] ^ $ * + ? | (); no captures, no {n,m}, no \d\w\s, no UTF-8, no icase; malloc
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1722 B.

engines.name: Ozan S. Yigit regex.c (1986, public domain)
engines.algorithm: compile to NFA byte program in static buffer; recursive pmatch; bitset classes
engines.features: . [] ranges/negation, * + closures, \(\) tags + \1-\9 backrefs, \< \>, ^ $; NO |, NO ?, NO {n,m}, NO \d\w\s, NO icase; globals (not reentrant)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1753 B + 128 data + 1168 bss. Software-Tools/Conroy-grep lineage; still shipped in a few hobby libcs.

engines.name: dietlibc libregex/rx.c
engines.algorithm: parse tree of matcher objects with function pointers ('poor man's OOP'), backtracking; POSIX regcomp/regexec API
engines.features: POSIX ERE-ish: | () captures, [] bracket incl. [:class:], * + ? {n,m}, ^ $, REG_ICASE, REG_NEWLINE; byte-wise; malloc
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2793 B (with dietlibc headers). GPL and POSIX semantics limit usefulness.

engines.name: PeterVranken/regExpEmbedded
engines.algorithm: separate compiler (host or target) -> compiled program; matcher is backtracking with NO recursion and caller-provided memory; compiled regexes exportable as C snippets
engines.features: ^ $ . [] ranges/negation, custom escapes (\d \h \a \A \s \i \I \xHH \N), ? * + {n} {m,M} with non-greedy, |, () grouping, capture groups via non-standard <...> syntax; ASCII; no icase
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: charSet 908 + compiler 1799 + matcher 1886 = ~4.6 KB (matcher alone ~2.8 KB). Split-compile idea; non-standard syntax.

engines.name: wernsey/wregex
engines.algorithm: compile to NFA program, backtracking executor
engines.features: ^ $ | () (?:) captures, * + ? {m,n} + lazy, [] ranges, backrefs, \b, \i\I case toggles, \d\w\s; ASCII; malloc
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: 5633+1260+550+62 = ~7.5 KB.

engines.name: torstenvl/trex (2022, not Demichelis)
engines.algorithm: Pike-style recursive matcher over the pattern with inline UTF-8 decode; classes via iswxxx/locale
engines.features: . ^ $ * + ? \d\s\w\x; NO [], NO (), NO |, NO {n,m}, boolean result only (no offsets); UTF-8 aware
engines.claimed_size: README: '<100 SLOC', '~3.5kb on macOS, ~4kb on Linux'
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=1516 B (pulls libc wctype).

engines.name: rolandbernard/regex (NFA->DFA)
engines.algorithm: regex -> NFA -> DFA, O(n) matching
engines.features: basic syntax; DFA (no captures); malloc
engines.notes: DFA construction needs heap and can blow up; no submatches. Not measured.

engines.name: jondurbin/dre2
engines.algorithm: 'fast lightweight' automaton-based with backtracking submatch
engines.features: icase, greedy, submatches
engines.notes: Toy/academic; not measured.

engines.name: Espruino RegExp (jswrap_regexp.c)
engines.algorithm: Pike-style recursive backtracking directly over the pattern string, operating on JsVar string iterators
engines.features: . ^ $ [] [^] \d\s\w, * + ?, | (top-level only: 'TODO | inside a group'), () captures (9), ignoreCase flag; NO {n,m}, NO lazy, 'Backreferences not supported'
engines.notes: Not standalone; shows what a shipping MCU JS interpreter settled for (~330 sloc). Not measured.

engines.name: Duktape RegExp
engines.algorithm: bytecode compiler + recursive backtracking executor with recursion limits (doc/regexp.rst)
engines.features: ES5 RegExp complete: {n,m}, lazy, backrefs, lookahead, \b, icase with canonicalization (DUK_USE_REGEXP_CANON_BITMAP ~300-400 B option)
engines.claimed_size: none (doc/low-memory.rst: undef DUK_USE_REGEXP_SUPPORT to save flash)
engines.notes: Not standalone (duk_internal). Not measured.

engines.name: JerryScript RegExp
engines.algorithm: parser -> bytecode -> backtracking executor
engines.features: ES5.1 RegExp (backrefs, lookahead, {n,m}, lazy, icase)
engines.notes: Not standalone. Not measured.

engines.name: Lua patterns (lstrlib.c) / nickgammon/Regexp Arduino port
engines.algorithm: recursive backtracking directly over the pattern (match/max_expand/min_expand)
engines.features: NOT regex: Lua patterns - . %a %d %s %w etc, [] sets, * + - (lazy) ?, () captures, %b, %f, ^ $; NO |, NO group quantifiers, NO {n,m}, NO icase, bytes only
engines.notes: Measured lstrlib.c Cortex-M4 pattern functions only: match 640 + match_class 176 + classend 108 + matchbracketclass 88 + capture/str helpers ~500 = ~1.5 KB. What Arduino/ESP32 users mostly use today; the size floor for 'usable' matching.

engines.name: regex-lite (Rust, comparison only)
engines.algorithm: Thompson NFA + Pike VM (pikevm.rs), no backtracking, O(m*n)
engines.features: regex-crate syntax minus Unicode classes: codepoint matching, ASCII-only \d\w\s, lazy, {n,m}, named groups, icase (ASCII), flags
engines.claimed_size: README: '94KB relative size increase' vs '565KB' for regex 1.9.0 (x86-64)
engines.notes: Out of scope (Rust) but the best documented 'lite regex' size datapoint: ~94 KB for the full feature set.

engines.name: SQLite ext/misc/regexp.c
engines.algorithm: recursive-descent compiler into a small op/arg array (RE_OP_*), then lockstep NFA simulation (Pike-style state sets, O(N*M), no backtracking); X{p,q} expanded by copying the sub-program
engines.features: * + ? {p,q} (greedy only), () grouping WITHOUT captures, |, ^ $ ., \uXXXX \xXX and C escapes, [] [^] ranges, \b, \w\W\d\D\s\S; UTF-8 code points; ASCII icase (re_next_char_nocase); boolean result only (no offsets); literal-prefix prefilter; sqlite3_malloc64 at compile, stack buffer at match for small NFAs
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=3282 B whole file; engine-only (minus SQL glue re_sql_func/init) = 2060 B. Smallest UTF-8-aware engine with {n,m}, \d\w\s and |, but a recogniser: no submatch offsets, no lazy. Proof that a lockstep NFA with classes + counted repetition fits in ~2 KB.

engines.name: Jim Tcl jimregexp.c (Spencer-1986 derived)
engines.algorithm: Spencer 1986 'book' design (linear NFA program of BRANCH/EXACTLY/... nodes, recursive backtracking regmatch) extended 2010 with REP/REPX/REPMIN/REPXMIN counted+minimal repeats and UTF-8; static state removed
engines.features: . ^ $ [] ranges/negation + [[:alpha:]] etc., \d\w\s (+ negations), \< \> word assertions, \xHH \uXXXX, * + ? {n,m} greedy AND minimal (*? +? ?? {n,m}?), |, () (?:) captures (100 parens), REG_ICASE (via utf8_tounicode_case), REG_NEWLINE; UTF-8 code points; no backrefs; malloc for program
engines.license: BSD-2-Clause (Jim Tcl LICENSE) + Spencer's original notice
engines.source_files: jimregexp.c jimregexp.h utf8.c utf8.h (jim.h + 3 stub headers for measurement)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=5174 B (+ utf8.c 104 B). Covers the whole 'modern basics' list with Perl-style backtracking; 2.6x the 2 KB target. Easy to lift out of Jim (needs only the utf8 helpers).

engines.name: mruby-hs-regexp (Spencer 1986 for mruby)
engines.algorithm: Spencer 1986 book library, allocator routed through mrb_malloc, flags in a regexp_info context
engines.features: . ^ $ [] ranges/negation, * + ?, |, () captures (9), IGNORECASE + MULTILINE flags; NO {n,m}, NO lazy, NO \d\w\s, NO UTF-8 (byte-wise)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=3219 B (stub mruby.h). What a scripting-language author reached for in 2013 when Oniguruma was 'too rich for embedded'. Feature-wise redundant with garyhouston/regexp.old.

engines.name: matp/tiny-regex (C11 Pike VM)
engines.algorithm: recursive-descent parser -> node array -> compiled program (re1-style Char/Any/Class/Split/Jmp/Save) executed by a Pike VM (regex_vm_pike.c, lockstep threads with captures)
engines.features: ^ $ . [] [^] ranges, ? * + {x,y} greedy and lazy (?? *? +? {x,y}?), () captures, |; NO \d\w\s shorthands (only \ literal escapes), NO (?:), NO UTF-8, NO icase; malloc via pluggable allocator struct
engines.source_files: src/regex_parse.c regex_compile.c regex_vm_pike.c regex_program.c regex_allocators.c + headers
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4: parse 1122 + compile 1094 + pike 590 + 28 = 2834 B. Clean small Pike VM with lazy and {x,y}; tests generated from Ruby's regex. Structural twin of jserv/cregex.

engines.name: Beariish/picomatch
engines.algorithm: single-pass compiler into a caller-sized bytecode block (pm_expsize/pm_compile, code stored after the struct), recursive matcher with 'limited backtracking' for quantifiers (match_loop/match_loop_lazy)
engines.features: ^ $ \b \B, () (?:) captures, [] [^] ranges, \s\S\w\W\d\D, \n\r\t\0\\, + +? * *? ? {n} {n,} {n,m}, |; no allocations, no global state; ASCII (ctype), NO icase, NO UTF-8
engines.notes: gcc 10.3 rejects its C23 label-before-declaration syntax; clang 21 -Os: Cortex-M4 text=4977 B, x86-64 7012 B. Closest 2025 newcomer to the spike's list minus UTF-8/icase; README calls its backtracking 'limited', expect divergences on nested quantifiers.

engines.name: alex-s168/tpre
engines.algorithm: host-side compiler (lexer/parser/re2fsm) emits the regex as a byte-array state machine; ~300-line runtime walks the FSM with a backtrack stack (SLOWARR)
engines.features: README: . \s\S\d\D\w\W, ranges, escapes, lazy (*? +?) and greedy (* +), ?, (?:), (?# comment), [] sets, |, () and (?'name') captures, ^ $; compiler options ignore_case and utf8 (tpre_compiler.h); NO {n,m} documented
engines.claimed_size: README: precompiled patterns 'reduce code size by a lot'
engines.source_files: runtime.c + include/ (compiler/*.c is a separate host tool)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 runtime.c text=922 B (tpre_matchn 576 B); runtime mallocs the group array. Same split-compile idea as regExpEmbedded; runtime user patterns would need the ~1.8 k-line compiler on target.

engines.name: GerbenAaltink/mrex (rmatch.h)
engines.algorithm: Kernighan/Pike matchhere over the pattern string plus a string-rewriting 'rmatch_compile' pre-pass; header-only
engines.features: . ^ + * (greedy) [abc]; README: '[abc] does NOT work with * +'; NO $ ? | () {n,m} \d\w\s, NO UTF-8, NO icase; malloc in compile/extract
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 engine functions ~1.56 KB (tests excluded). Toy; listed only because GitHub topic 'regex-engine' surfaces it.

engines.name: eriknyquist/librxvm
engines.algorithm: two-stage compiler (lex -> stage1 -> stage2 VM code) and non-backtracking NFA VM (Pike-style); Boyer-Moore-Horspool prefilter for file search
engines.features: + * ? {n} {n,m} {,m} {n,} (greedy; non-greedy and case-insensitive are global flags), [] classes/ranges, () grouping, |, ^ $ ., escapes; ASCII only; NO submatch captures (rxvm_search returns overall start/end only), NO \d\w\s in README; malloc
engines.claimed_size: README: configure options 'shave off ~40% ... (around 20K in my case)' (x86, unverified)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 engine sum = 7688 B. Non-backtracking, so lazy is a flag, not per-quantifier.

engines.name: monolifed/tiny-regex-mod (kokke single-header fork)
engines.algorithm: kokke design (token array + backtracking matchpattern) as a single header with separate greedy/lazy quantifier matchers
engines.features: kokke set + {m,n} {m} {m,} and lazy ?? *? +? {m,n}?, '.' excludes \r\n, caller-owned compiled object; still NO |, NO groups/captures, NO UTF-8, NO icase
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=2708 B incl. tre_print+typenames ~275 B -> ~2.4 KB. Most popular kokke variant that adds lazy + {m,n}; Lua-driven tests.

engines.name: gyrovorbis/tiny-regex-c (kokke fork, 2026)
engines.algorithm: kokke design with byte-packed symbols, user-supplied compiled-pattern storage (re_compile_to/re_size) and a stringifier
engines.features: kokke set + working {n} {,m} {n,} {n,m} (merged pending PRs), \xHH; NO |, NO groups, NO lazy, NO UTF-8, NO icase; README: recursion and print() 'broke'
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 text=3090 B incl. re_string stringifier ~480 B -> ~2.6 KB engine.

engines.name: MicroQuickJS regexp (Bellard 2025, inside mquickjs.c)
engines.algorithm: libregexp descendant embedded in mquickjs.c (lines ~15711-17557): direct bytecode emission (REOP_*), register-stack allocation, backtracking interpreter lre_exec
engines.features: ES5-level: classes/ranges, \d\w\s\b, * + ? {n,m} greedy+lazy, | () (?:) captures, lookahead (?= (?!, backrefs, flags i m g (s y u accepted); NO lookbehind, NO named groups, NO Unicode properties; matches code points; case folding ASCII-only (README)
engines.claimed_size: README: whole JS engine ~100 kB ROM (ARM Thumb-2), 10 kB RAM
engines.source_files: not standalone: part of mquickjs.c (JSContext, JS byte arrays)
engines.notes: Measured Cortex-M4 (whole TU, regexp functions summed): compiler+interpreter = 7100 B (lre_exec 3306, re_parse_alternative 2396) + ~900 B JS glue. Bellard's answer to 'JS regex for MCUs': the spike's envelope plus lookahead/backrefs at ~7 KB.

engines.name: Tcl regex / hsrex (Henry Spencer 1998)
engines.algorithm: Spencer 1998 hybrid: NFA over 'colors', DFA-driven matching with submatch resolution by re-running sub-DFAs (rege_dfa.c)
engines.features: AREs: POSIX + {n,m}, non-greedy, lookahead, backrefs, classes, Unicode (Tcl_UniChar)
engines.source_files: regcomp.c regc_*.c regexec.c rege_dfa.c regerror.c regfree.c
engines.notes: Scale reference: the 'other' Spencer engine (also PostgreSQL's). Not measured.

engines.name: katef/libfsm
engines.algorithm: regex -> NFA -> minimised DFA (libre + libfsm) with C/asm code generation; matching by DFA tables
engines.features: several dialects (PCRE subset, POSIX, glob, ...), no backtracking; capture support via DFA capture resolution (unverified)
engines.notes: Scale reference for 'compile to DFA offline': generated matchers are tiny, the compiler is not embeddable. Not measured.

observations: Landscape (55 projects opened, 51 catalogued): under ~3 KB on Cortex-M4 everything is a Kernighan/Pike-style backtracker over a token array (kokke 1.4 KB, subreg 1.7, slre 1.9, zeta-zero 1.9, tiny-regex-mod 2.4, ximtech 2.4, gyrovorbis 2.6, T-Rex 2.9) and each drops at least two required features (groups+alternation, {n,m}, lazy, UTF-8 or icase); none is leftmost-first-correct with captures. The VM family (re1.5 ~1.9 KB compile+backtrack, SQLite regexp.c 2.1, cregex 2.6, matp/tiny-regex 2.8, Plan 9 3.2, pikevm 3.7) has correct nested groups; SQLite's is the only ~2 KB engine with UTF-8 + {n,m} + \d\w\s + |, but returns a boolean. Engines covering the whole 'modern basics' list (picomatch ~5 KB clang, jimregexp 5.2, mujs 5.4, mquickjs 7.1, Remimu 7.3, wregex 7.5, librxvm 7.7, QuickJS 13, musl/TRE 13) are 2.5-7x over the 2 KB target, so a 1-2 KB engine with the full list has no existing proof point; the budget sits between kokke-class and re1.5-class. Measurements (Cortex-M4 -Os, compile-only, PROTOCOL.md) with exact commands: $S/survey/measure/*.txt and $S/engines/<name>/BUILD.txt. Licensing blockers: slre GPL2/commercial, dietlibc GPL2, regExpEmbedded LGPL3; everything else MIT/BSD/zlib/ISC/0BSD/public domain. Not located: 'picore' (closest match Beariish/picomatch 2025), 'jsre' (only Nim std/jsre; kmarius/jsregexp is QuickJS-for-Lua), 'mini-re'; 'ure' (Leisher 1997 Unicode DFA, UCS-2) only on a dead NMSU FTP URL (unverified). GitHub topics regex/regex-engine (l=c) also surface toys/assignments omitted here (Comprosoft Regex-C 'not done', yashgawankar, Joku1806/regen 'no testing', Zer0-Bug, steynvl/rel). Sources people consult: HN 25281977/44327833, Embedded Artistry 2019 (C++ CTRE), MicroPython 'ure' docs, Tasmota Berry (re1.5), Arduino Regexp (Lua patterns). picomatch needs C23 (gcc 10.3 fails); 9front not measured (Plan 9 headers); rsc/re1 measured with bison-generated parser.
